headline: Recommended edits to draft impact fee ordinance; agreed to seek $50,000 for Police Station and Middle School fee study.
summary: Staff presented draft changes to the impact fee ordinance, including several waivers. Edits were recommended, and staff will revise the draft and develop a concept for a possible impact fee credit for sustainability features. The next meeting is November 17 at 4PM.
decisions: Recommended edits to the draft impact fee ordinance amendments, covering six waiver and priority project sections.
Agreed to seek funding for a $50,000 impact fee study and recommended using a City reserve fund for the appropriation.
Approved the minutes of September 1, 2026, as corrected. The motion passed unanimously.

AD-HOC IMPACT FEE REVIEW COMMITTEE 
Minutes 
October 28, 2026 @ 4:00PM 
City Hall Large 2nd Floor Conference Room 
41 Green Street, Concord NH 03301 
 
Attendees: 
 Byron Champlin, Mayor 
 Judith Kurtz, At-Large City Councilor 
 Brent Todd, Ward 1 City Councilor, Chair 
 Jeff Foote, Ward 10 City Councilor 
 
Absent 
 Bill Norton, Resident, representative of the Greater Concord Chamber of Commerce  
 Chuck Gilboy, guest / member of the Economic Development Advisory Committee 
 
Public: 
 None 
 
Staff: 
 Matt Walsh, Deputy City Manager, Development 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:00PM   
 
1. Minutes of September 1, 2026 
Two typographical errors were noted for correction.  Judith Kurtz moved adoption of the minutes as 
corrected.  Jeff Foote seconded.  The motion carried unanimously. 
 
2. Discussion – Estimated Cost and Schedule for Development of Police Station and Concord Middle 
School Impact Fees 
Mr. Walsh noted that, during its September 1, 2026 meeting, the Committee directed staff to research the 
potential cost to engage a qualified consultant to confirm preliminary capacity analyses for the new Police 
Station and Middle School Projects, as well as prepare necessary methodologies and calculations to 
establish impact fees to support these two capital improvement projects. Mr. Walsh stated that, per a 
discussion he had with one of the City’s consultants, he would recommend a budget of $50,000 for this 
effort. Once a consultant is selected, the project would take approximately 6-9 months to complete. 
 
Discussion ensued about when and how to seek a potential appropriation from City Council, as well as 
potential funding sources to support the appropriation.  
 
 
CITY OF CONCORD 
New Hampshire’s Main Street™ 
41 Green Street, Concord NH 03301 
(603) 225-8570
Page 2 of 3 
 
It was the consensus of the Committee to seek funding for this purpose simultaneously with presenting the 
Committee’s proposed amendments to the Impact Fee ordinance. The Committee also recommended that 
staff use an appropriate City reserved fund to finance the required appropriation. 
 
3. Review Draft Impact Fee Ordinance Amendments 
Mr. Walsh presented the draft proposed amendments to the Committee.  Mr. Walsh reported that the Legal 
Department also recently had the opportunity to review the draft ordinance, and he provided their feedback 
during his presentation. 
 
The Committee completed a page by page review of the Ordinance, and was very supportive of the draft 
proposed amendments prepared by staff. 
 
Upon review, the Committee recommended the following edits: 
 
1. Waiver for Market Rate Housing in the Central Business Performance District:  
a. Provide a preamble explaining the intent of the waiver; 
b. That a covenant be added that dwelling units will remain “market rate” in perpetuity; and, 
c. Revise to provide guidance to the Planning Board on how to process and award the waiver 
request. 
2. Waiver for Priority Nonresidential Uses:   
a. Provide a preamble explaining the intent of the waiver; 
b. Expand the list of land uses be expanded to include “technology”; and, 
c. Revise to provide guidance to the Planning Board on how to process and award the waiver 
request. 
3. Waiver for Redevelopment of Historically Significant Structures:  
a. Provide a preamble explaining the intent of the waiver; 
b. Clarify that the waiver is available City-wide to all qualifying historic structures; 
c. Add bonus of additional 5% for projects that are redeveloped in a manner which complies 
with the US Secretary of the Interior Standards; require review of project at time of 
Certificate of Occupancy (when impact fees are due and payable) to confirm project 
conformed with said requirements; and, 
d. Revise to provide guidance to the Planning Board on how to process and award the waiver 
request. 
4.  Waiver for Properties Involving Remediation of Soil or Groundwater 
a. Provide a preamble explaining the intent of the waiver; 
b. Allow for additional waiver beyond 25% based upon demonstrable need (staff to develop 
language); and, 
c. Revise to provide guidance to the Planning Board on how to process and award the waiver 
request. 
5. Waiver for Redevelopment of Vacant or Blighted Properties 
a. Provide a preamble explaining the intent of the waiver; 
b. Allow for additional waiver beyond 25% based upon demonstrable need (staff to develop 
language); 
c. Review use of the term “gross living area” in this section; modify definitions of floor area 
and gross floor area as might be warranted; and, 
d. Revise to provide guidance to the Planning Board on how to process and award the waiver 
request. 
6. City Priority Development Projects 
a. Revise to provide guidance to the Planning Board on how to process and award the waiver 
request.
Page 3 of 3 
 
The Committee also expressed interest in a potential impact fee credit for development that incorporate 
sustainability features. Discussion ensued about potential criteria to qualify for any such waiver (such as 
LEED Certification) and potential challenges with implementation thereof.  Staff will work to develop a 
potential concept for the Committee’s review. 
 
4. Next Steps and Future Meeting Dates 
Per the Committee’s input, Staff will prepare additional revisions to the draft proposed ordinance 
amendment.  The Committee will meet on November 17th at 4PM to review.   
 
5. Adjourn  
The meeting adjourned at 6:20PM. 
 
Respectfully Submitted; 
 
 
Matthew R. Walsh 
Deputy City Manager – Development
